scope: Targeted review of concrete WWW main-conference examples, not a survey of venue-wide chart frequencies.

design_decision: A monochrome grouped comparison table with two method rows and one count-difference row. App and independent Browser each retain timezone and language columns. Total detections and normal alarms remain visible. Only changed detection cells are bold.
adaptation_not_copied_from_sources: The count-difference row is a task-specific addition; literal n/N values preserve our small sample sizes. Bold marks changes, not statistical significance. No source's experimental conclusions are transferred to this study.
limits: Source text/table structures and WWW venue identities were verified. This is not a claim of exact typography reproduction or of venue-wide requirements. Output is a discussion draft, not a final paper-scale validation.
english_caption: Saved direction-specific detection counts for Full App and Full App plus the retained cross-endpoint timezone check (C1). The five additional detections occur only for Browser timezone modifications; App timezone detections are retained and both language families remain undetected. The last row reports changes in counts, not percentage points. All displayed counts agree across the three frozen configurations and are shown once. On the 46 normal positions both methods produce no alarms or unknown/failed outputs. These 60 positions have development-use history. On the separate historical MTC evaluation material (144 and 117 positions), alarm counts are unchanged within each configuration while unknown outputs increase from 14 to 17.
